title: FieldOps Mobile
shortDescription: An iOS and Android application for field crews working without connectivity, with conflict-safe sync and photographic proof of work.
fullDescription: Field crews were completing jobs on paper because every previous app assumed a connection. FieldOps treats offline as the normal case: the entire day's work is available on the device, evidence is captured locally, and synchronisation resolves conflicts deterministically when signal returns. Dispatch sees progress as it syncs rather than at the end of the day.

challenge.summary: Crews worked in basements, rural sites and industrial buildings with no reliable signal. Two previous applications had been rejected by the field team.

points.title: Work lost on failure

points.title: Billing disputes over proof
points.description: Proof of work was inconsistent, which caused billing disputes.

solution.summary: We designed for the disconnected case first and treated connectivity as an optimisation, not a requirement.

points.title: Explicit conflict rules

points.title: Resumable evidence uploads

objectives: Keep a whole job usable with no connectivity at all
Never lose completed work, even on a failed submission
Sync proof of work reliably to the office
Ship new job types without an app store review
Win over the crews who rejected earlier apps
clientOverview: A field services operation whose crews spend most of the working day without connectivity. Earlier mobile attempts had lost work on failed submissions and been abandoned in favour of paper — which pushed a day of lag and transcription errors into the office and kept billing disputes alive over inconsistent proof of work.
conclusion: Crews now run entire jobs offline with the device as the source of truth, and completed work syncs reliably — including photographic proof, with resumable uploads that survive poor coverage. New job types ship from the server without app store reviews, and the interaction model, shaped by a two-week pilot with the crews themselves, was adopted where earlier apps had been rejected.
